evidence_detail: 22 distinct InChIKeys, 0 duplicates at molecule level, and the 3-gate intersection is byte-hashed and reproducible -- that part holds. But the pool is NOT 22 independent observations at source level: 16 DOIs, of which 13 contribute exactly 1 molecule and one paper (10.1021/je600515j) contributes 5/22 = 22.7% (2-amino-2-methylpropan-1-ol, 1,2-propanediol, triethanolamine, N-(2-hydroxypropyl)-2-hydroxy-1-propanamine, diethanolamine). 7/22 rows pool several contributing measurements yet every row declares n_independent_experiments=1. Temperature is not homogeneous: 6 set-points over a 10 K span (293.15-303.15) with no per-molecule T replication, so the T-correction cannot be validated (Spearman eps vs T = +0.076). Range restriction: the 22 are only 30.1% of the 73-molecule model-ready universe (pool mean eps 17.32, sd 12.76 vs model-ready mean 23.49, sd 26.11), so it is a quality-selected subset, not a chemical sample. Pool size is meaningless for E6: k=3 uses 13.6% of the pool, C(22,3)=1540, and swapping one molecule into the Top-3 moves reported regret by up to 8.10 epsilon units (1-methylimidazole) -- larger than the whole reported effect. B04's own report already refuses to call this a training set, so the correct action is a further downgrade, not a re-run.

Reproduced the published numbers exactly (X0 17.446507, X0+X1 17.286655, bias -16.72/-17.01, E4 LOMO 17.2375). Root cause: ridge_fit solves (Z'Z+lam*I)b = Z'y on standardised Z with NO intercept column. Every column of Z sums to zero on the training rows, so Zb has training mean exactly 0 for ANY b (verified: mean(fitted) = 2.9e-15, mean(y) = 17.3155, in-sample bias = -17.3155 at both lam=0 and lam=1). The estimator is structurally incapable of representing ybar = 17.3155. Corroboration across independent outputs: all five published MAEs (17.4465, 17.2867, 17.2375, 17.3192, 17.2559) lie within 0.131 of mean|y| = mean(y) = 17.3155, which is exactly what a predictor emitting ~0.3-0.6 on strictly positive labels must give. The labels are all positive (min eps 1.93), so mean|y| == mean(y) and the 'baseline MAE 10.806' being BETTER than every model is a consequence of the offset, not of descriptor content. One-line fix (add the training mean back, equivalent to fit_intercept=True): X0 10.232, X0+X1 6.492 vs constant 10.806. Nested-CV with lambda chosen inside the fold (no test leakage) gives X0 10.485, X0+X1 7.138, electronic-only block 6.313, dipole alone 6.447. Permutation nulls (5000 perms): X0 p=0.078, X0+X1 p=0.0004, dipole-only p=0.0004. So claim A ('both models worse than a constant baseline') is false, and claim B ('electronic descriptors add no detectable value') is false too: Delta MAE = -3.740, bootstrap 95% CI [-7.32, -0.26], 98.3% of bootstrap replicates negative, X0+X1 better on 15/22 molecules. Dipole alone has Pearson r = 0.808 with epsilon. The report's statement 'this is not a tuning problem' is the exact claim falsified here. Note the lam=1 over-regularisation hypothesis in the mandate is NOT the explanation: lam=0.01/0.1/1/10/100 all give X0 17.8/17.5/17.4/17.1/17.2 without the intercept, i.e. the offset dominates any lambda choice.

E4 uses the same no-intercept solver on 11 columns (it drops total_energy_hartree but keeps the other 4 electronic descriptors), so all its error levels are offset by -16.94. Reproduced LOO MAE 17.2375 (published 17.2375, |diff| = 3e-5), bias -16.9385. With the intercept restored: leave-one-family-out MAE = 6.315 vs constant baseline 10.806, and 5 of the 6 measurable families now BEAT their train-mean baseline (alcohol 2.13 vs 5.90, dinitrile 1.74 vs 11.56, carbonate 2.26 vs 15.76, ketone 4.81 vs 8.14, unclassified 4.27 vs 18.72; only primary_secondary_amine fails, 8.76 vs 6.38). The published claim was 'only 1/6 families beat baseline', which is the opposite count. B07 re-imports this same E4 file (sha256 4180d8aa...) and quotes it as evidence, so the error propagates. Structural caveat that survives either way: 4/11 families have a single member and 5 more have two, so the 6 'measurable' families rest on only 19 molecules total; and primary_secondary_amine, the one family that still fails, is 4 molecules of which ALL 4 come from the single DOI 10.1021/je600515j, so its failure and its success are both source-confounded. E4's own 'unclassified' bucket holds 4 molecules that are actually 3 n-alkanes plus sulfolane, i.e. the family taxonomy is coarser than the chemistry it claims to stratify.

First, E6's arithmetic is NOT affected by the intercept bug, which is why HOLD and not FAIL: adding a constant to every prediction is a monotone transform, so the Top-3 set is identical under the bug and under the fix (sulfolane, N-(2-hydroxypropyl)-2-hydroxy-1-propanamine, 1,4,7,10,13-pentaoxacyclopentadecane; mean eps 24.45, regret 13.38). Second, the p-value is confirmed, not a Monte Carlo artefact: exact enumeration of all C(22,3) = 1540 subsets gives 242 subsets with mean >= 24.45, so p = 242/1540 = 0.1571 (published 0.16 from 2000 MC draws; MC reproduced 0.160). The mandate's worry that 2000 permutations is too few is unfounded, and p is NOT floored: the oracle subset alone yields p = 1/1540 = 0.00065, so a perfect ranker would be detected at alpha=0.05. Third -- and this is the real defect -- p = 0.157 is a NON-REJECTION, and the report converts it into the EQUIVALENCE claim 'indistinguishable from random'. That is not licensed. The point estimate sits at the 84.3rd percentile of every possible random Top-3 (model mean 24.45 vs random mean 17.32 vs oracle 37.83), i.e. the model is better than 84% of random draws; the one-sided p is 0.157 for 'random >= model' but 0.843 for 'model >= random'. With n=22 a TOST-style equivalence margin was never pre-specified, so 'no detectable value' and 'indistinguishable' must be downgraded to 'not demonstrated superior at this power'. The report's own status field INSUFFICIENT_POWER is correct and should be the only conclusion carried forward.

THREE independent failures, so this is NOT descriptor blindness.
(1) The premise is false at the modelling level. Tanimoto = 1.000 comes from a 2048-bit Morgan-2 PRESENCE fingerprint, which is known to collide on homologous n-alkanes: nonane (C9H20, 9 heavy atoms) and heptane (C7H16, 7 heavy atoms) are different molecules that land on the same bits. Verified: radius 2 -> 4 molecules at similarity 1.0; radius 3 -> 0; radius 4 -> 0; RDKit path fingerprint -> 0. The fingerprint is NOT the model's input anyway: the model consumes 11 continuous RDKit/xTB descriptors, and for nonane vs heptane 7 of the 11 differ by more than 1% (heavy_atom_count 9 vs 7, molecular_volume_A3 162.05 vs 128.66, molar_volume 9.76e-5 vs 7.75e-5, dipole 0.040 vs 0.053, polarizability_A3 16.33 vs 12.87, homo_lumo_gap 12.91 vs 13.12). For the dinitrile pair, 6 of 11 differ. So 'the descriptors cannot distinguish them' does not follow.
(2) If the model really were blind it would be FORCED to emit equal predictions, and the irreducible error would be half the true gap. Instead it emits nonane -20.596 vs heptane -14.929, a predicted gap of 5.667 against a true gap of 0.050 -- it EXAGGERATES the difference by 113x. The dinitrile pair is predicted 9.334 vs 7.835 (gap 1.498 vs true 3.770). A blind model cannot exaggerate; a mis-levelled model can.
(3) The published 19.4791 is a global-offset number. mean|y| = mean(y) = 17.3155 because every label is positive, and the published per-molecule errors are 22.5762 / 16.8593 / 16.6064 / 21.8746. A ZERO-descriptor constant predictor scores 15.34 / 15.39 / 8.62 / 12.39 on those same four molecules, MAE 12.935. So the model is 1.51x WORSE than using no descriptors at all, and beats the mean predictor on 0 of the 4. That is worse-than-trivial miscalibration, not a similarity-localised failure.
(4) The fix confirms it: adding back the training mean gives nonane -2.551 (err 4.531), heptane 3.119 (err 1.189), octanedinitrile 26.238 (err 0.298), heptanedinitrile 24.561 (err 5.149) -- MAE 2.792 vs the mean predictor's 12.935, and now beats the mean predictor on 4/4 molecules. On the whole 22 the four are no longer the worst group: under the fixed model their mean error is 2.792 versus 7.676 for the other 18, and three of them (octanedinitrile rank 22/22, heptane 20/22, nonane 14/22) become among the BEST-predicted molecules in the pool -- the exact reverse of the published ranking. A single scalar correction fitted out-of-fold and using no molecule information removes 60.9% of the reported 17.2375 error, which bounds how much of the 'decisive' evidence can be descriptor content at all. The correct residual statement is the opposite of the report's: the descriptor set DOES resolve these pairs (volume, polarizability and heavy-atom count differ), and the published errors were the global level. The claim as written ('proves the descriptors cannot resolve chemically distinct liquids', flagged as '本轮最重要的结论') must be RETRACTED, not reworded: the sign of the evidence reverses.

Reproduced the published ladder exactly (sigma 0/0.5/1/2/4/8 -> MAE 17.2375/17.2427/17.2488/17.2853/17.4348/17.9308, regret 13.38/13.38/13.38/12.898/10.933/10.561). Two findings.
(a) The ladder stops at sigma=8, which is almost exactly where regret bottoms out. Extended to sigma = 8/12/16/32/64/128/256 the regret goes 10.29 -> 11.52 -> 12.83 -> 15.74 -> 18.02 -> 19.28 -> 19.80, climbing monotonically toward the pure-random asymptote (oracle 37.83 - pool mean 17.32 = 20.51). So 'regret decreases with noise' is false as a monotone statement: the ladder contains a bounded dip and the report sampled only the dip. The same shape appears with the intercept fixed (dip to 11.04 at sigma=8, then back up to 19.45 at sigma=128), so this truncation artefact is independent of the intercept bug.
(b) The dip itself is real and seed-robust -- 60/60 seeds show regret falling at sigma=8 (mean delta -2.99, sd 0.25) and 60/60 show recovery at sigma=64 (mean delta +4.67). So it is not a seed artefact, and the mandate's robustness worry does not land.
(c) The inference drawn from it does not survive. The gate file lists '加入噪声反而改善 regret, 说明预测对筛选有害' as a supported conclusion and the verdict string is REGRET_DECOUPLED_AND_ANTI_CORRELATED. This contradicts E6 in the same report: E6's model Top-3 mean is 24.45, which is the 84.3rd percentile of all 1540 random Top-3 sets, and the one-sided p for 'random >= model' is only 0.157. A predictor whose Top-3 beats 84% of random draws is not 'harmful for screening'. What the dip actually shows is that the model's ranking is over-confident near the top: it ranks 1-methylimidazole (true eps 39.78, true rank 2) 5th and heptanedinitrile (29.71, rank 3) 6th, so random perturbation sometimes promotes them (noise-at-8 Top-3 sits at the 91.8th percentile, above the model's own). That is a rank-calibration defect, not evidence of anti-correlation. The 'harmful' verdict must be retracted; the defensible residual claim is 'ranking is imperfect and noise happens to help at moderate sigma'.
